description: ASTROGRON is a multidisciplinary team of six reimagining farming as an interconnected system where every harvest shapes the next. Combining NASA Earth observations, climate and water modeling, and five-year optimization, we transparently evaluate smarter crop rotations. We model how each crop shifts soil nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to build productive, sustainable, and resilient farms. ASTROGRON — Traceable Science from Space to Soil.
summary:
ASTROGRON is a scientific research system that helps people understand what Earth-observation evidence can and cannot tell us about a farm. It combines traceable NASA POWER historical climate data, available soil evidence, and agricultural constraints to compare multi-year crop alternatives under declared assumptions. Every result is tied to an identifiable analysis, and an AI assistant explains what the scientific engine found rather than replacing it.

For the Field Shift challenge, ASTROGRON supports farm adaptation with NASA data by showing which conclusions the evidence supports, which depend on stated assumptions, and which are blocked because critical evidence is missing. A missing soil measurement is never turned into an invented number.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

ASTROGRON turns Earth-observation data into transparent, evidence-guided agricultural decisions. In an interactive Earth explorer, users select an agricultural location. For supported research cases, ASTROGRON combines historical NASA POWER climate data, available soil evidence and agricultural constraints to evaluate multi-year crop rotation alternatives, water and resource limits, and historical climate scenarios over a five-year horizon.

Unlike a typical AI chatbot, ASTROGRON keeps scientific computation separate from AI-generated explanation. Every result links to an identifiable analysis, documented assumptions and traceable evidence. Users can compare alternatives, download scientific reports and discuss findings with an evidence-grounded AI assistant. Each conclusion is marked Supported, Conditional or Blocked. When essential evidence is missing, the system says so instead of inventing a recommendation.

ASTROGRON also includes a public awareness component. Healthy soil depends on choices made by everyone, not only by farmers. Through social media accounts, we share short, plain-language posts, infographics and videos that connect NASA Earth-observation data to everyday life. These explain how air, water and soil pollution, plastic waste, chemical runoff and careless disposal affect the soil that grows our food, and what ordinary people can do about it. The content is built from the same evidence rules as the platform: every claim is tied to a source, and uncertainty is stated openly.

What benefits does it have, and what is the intended impact?

A farming decision can shape far more than one harvest. Crop choice, water availability, soil condition and climate variability all affect decisions for years, yet farmers often face fragmented information, incomplete measurements and uncertainty about which conclusions to trust. ASTROGRON makes scientific evidence understandable and actionable within clearly defined limits. Farmers, agricultural advisors, researchers, cooperatives and development organizations can use it to explore alternatives, understand constraints and see which information still needs verification.

The awareness component widens that impact beyond the farm. Our aim is to help everyday people see their link to the food they eat. Reducing pollution, cutting waste, supporting responsible food choices and protecting local land and water all help keep soil healthy, and healthy soil supports better crops. By turning satellite data into simple, shareable stories, we hope to encourage small, practical actions in homes and communities. We do not claim that a post alone improves soil. The intended impact is informed, motivated communities who support, and benefit from, better agricultural outcomes.

What tools, coding languages, hardware and software did you use?

  • Data and imagery: NASA POWER historical climate data, NASA GIBS imagery, Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery from EOX, and OpenStreetMap-based geographic information. SoilGrids is evaluated where available, subject to evidence and integration limits.
  • Scientific computing: Python, PCSE/WOFOST crop and water modeling, Google OR-Tools for constrained optimization, and NumPy and Pandas.
  • Web development: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Python backend APIs, persistent scientific job queues and automated PDF reporting.
  • AI assistant: Google Gemini API for evidence-grounded explanations, with a local evidence-based fallback. The verified demonstration supports offline explanations. Live cloud inference depends on availability and data-protection restrictions.
  • Awareness and outreach: Social media platforms for publishing educational content, with graphics and short videos made from NASA imagery and the platform’s evidence outputs.
  • Hardware and infrastructure: Standard laptops without dedicated GPUs, CPU-based processing, a modular backend, and Cloudflare HTTPS for remote demonstration.

How is your project creative?

What if the most valuable feature of an intelligent system were knowing when not to answer? Instead of producing confident conclusions from incomplete information, ASTROGRON separates evidence-supported analysis, conditional results and conclusions that must stay blocked. A missing measurement is never silently replaced by an invented one, and a research scenario is never presented as a guaranteed harvest or profit.

Our second creative step is to pair this scientific rigor with public storytelling. Most agricultural tools reach only specialists. By bringing the same honest, evidence-first approach to social media, we aim to make Earth-observation science part of everyday conversation, so ordinary people can see how their own choices connect to the soil and the food on their plates.

What factors did your team consider?

Scientific reliability, geographic coverage, responsible AI and usability guided our work. We considered the spatial resolution of satellite and climate datasets, recognizing that regional estimates cannot fully represent individual fields. We distinguished measured information from modeled estimates and declared assumptions. We also weighed crop suitability, soil calibration, irrigation access, water rights and pesticide regulations, and we separated the computational engine from the AI explanation layer to guard against unsupported conclusions.

For the awareness work, we considered accuracy and tone: avoiding exaggerated or fear-based claims, citing sources, keeping language simple, and not suggesting that individual actions alone solve pollution or guarantee better harvests.

Our prototype demonstrates research workflows using verified historical datasets and explicitly identified illustrative assumptions, and some examples are cached for reproducible demonstrations. ASTROGRON is a research prototype, not a field-validated agricultural advisory service. Further development requires local measurements, broader verified crop coverage and independent field validation.

Guiding principle: From orbital observations to grounded decisions, with evidence at every step.
